mfg1-mechanical-lesson-078.title: Read information from coordinate and surface-roughness measuring machines
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-078.objective: Read information from coordinate and surface-roughness measuring machines, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: In a contact-type example, a coordinate measuring machine, CMM, reads the coordinates where a probe touches the target, then calculates lengths, angles, geometric tolerances and similar properties. One point of contact does not automatically guarantee the whole part’s shape. Check fixing, coordinate references, measurement points and the plan.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: A stylus-type surface-roughness instrument traces the surface and converts vertical stylus motion into a signal describing its unevenness. Values such as Ra require measurement conditions and a specified location. A hole-location result from a CMM cannot simply become a surface-roughness result.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: A measurement report links the instrument, reference, measured location and evaluation parameter. Roughness and geometric shape, and coordinate values and acceptance judgments, are different information. Ask the responsible person to confirm the plan for inaccessible areas or surfaces where contact may affect the result.

terms.reading: さんじげんそくていき
terms.meaning: A machine evaluating dimensions and geometric properties from coordinates and related information.
The part detecting a target’s position and related features.
A contact tip tracing a surface.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-079.title: Protect gauge-block measuring faces and store them correctly
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-079.objective: Protect gauge-block measuring faces and store them correctly, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: In a rectangular gauge-block example, the length between two opposing precision measuring faces provides the reference. Do not assume every visible face has the same role. Joining blocks by close adhesion is also called wringing. This is different from adding lengths with paper or dirt left between them.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: After use, remove fingerprints and other contamination, then apply the specified corrosion protection and storage. Do not file away a burr on a measuring face with an ordinary file. Even if the source describes a specialized treatment, confirm the authorized operator and instrument procedure. A damaged reference affects later results set from it.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: A master ring is used to set internal-diameter comparison, while plug and ring limit gauges are used for GO/NO-GO judgments. Do not determine use solely from whether the measuring face is inside or outside. Check whether it is a master or limit gauge, its identification and its certification or inspection condition. Keep these roles separate in storage too.

terms.meaning: Bringing precision measuring faces into close contact.
Preventing rust.
A face used as a dimensional reference or for contact with a target.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-080.title: Read line weights and the roles of special lines
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-080.objective: Read line weights and the roles of special lines, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: Line weights include thin, thick and extra-thick lines; the source describes their relative ratio as 1:2:4. Even when paper or printing changes, distinguish visible outlines from dimension lines. Read solid, dashed, single-dash-dot and double-dash-dot patterns together with their weight.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: A thin double-dash-dot phantom line may show adjacent parts, fixture positions, moved positions, or shapes before and after machining as reference information. A break line marks an omitted boundary; a cutting-plane line identifies the section position and viewing direction; hatching relates to cut material. Do not machine a referenced phantom shape as the part’s current finished outline.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Scale is the ratio between drawing size and actual size. Distinguish enlargement examples such as 2:1 or 5:1 from reduction examples such as 1:2 or 1:5. Remembering line-weight ratios or recommended scales does not authorize filling in an unreadable drawing. Request a readable approved drawing when copying has obscured line types.

terms.meaning: A line showing a reference position, shape or similar information.
A line marking an omitted portion or related boundary.
A line-weight category heavier than thin and thick lines.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-081.title: Match symbols for spheres, squares, chamfers and holes
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-081.objective: Match symbols for spheres, squares, chamfers and holes, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: The symbol φ represents diameter, Sφ sphere diameter, R radius, SR sphere radius, and □ a square’s side. CR denotes a controlled radius. For arc length, read the auxiliary arc symbol and dimension-line form, keeping it distinct from straight chord length. Similar symbols do not make a circle and sphere, or radius and diameter, identical.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: C indicates a 45-degree chamfer and t indicates thickness. There are also symbols for conical chamfers, spotfaces or counterbores, countersinks and depths. Match the drawing target with nominal tool sizes and machining instructions. For example, C2 cannot be independently changed to an arbitrary rounded R2 feature regardless of direction or angle.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Symbols may be omitted where the drawing and dimension line make a radius or diameter clear. A radius obtainable from other dimensions may be given as a reference dimension. Even when a symbol is omitted, check the target. Do not guess unreadable symbols to decide hole depth or seating-face shape; ask about the original drawing.

terms.meaning: The diameter of a sphere.
Removing an edge to a specified shape.
Machining a hole entrance or similar area to a specified form.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-082.title: Organize the source’s geometric-tolerance types by shape, orientation and position
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-082.objective: Organize the source’s geometric-tolerance types by shape, orientation and position, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: The source lists straightness, flatness, roundness, cylindricity, profile of a line and profile of a surface. Separate the targets: a line, plane, circle, cylinder and profile. Checking roundness in one location does not mean the shape of the entire cylinder has been checked.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Parallelism, perpendicularity and angularity concern orientation; position, concentricity, coaxiality and symmetry provide distinctions for position relationships and related requirements. The source also lists circular runout and total runout. Even similarly round symbols differ in target, required references and tolerance zones. Do not substitute one characteristic simply because you remember another symbol’s name.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: A tolerance frame combines the characteristic symbol, value and necessary references. An arrow identifying a surface may be attached differently from an axis indication. Follow the drawing’s applicable standard and measurement plan. Do not transfer names or symbols from an older source to a new drawing without confirmation. Show the reference and arrow when asking about an unclear target.

terms.meaning: A geometric characteristic dealing with the form of a cylinder.
A geometric characteristic dealing with orientation at a specified angle.
A geometric characteristic dealing with overall runout.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-083.title: Match metallic luster, thermal conductivity and melting point to use
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-083.objective: Match metallic luster, thermal conductivity and melting point to use, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: Metallic luster concerns reflection of light. Oxidation or other surface changes alter appearance, so shine alone does not identify a material. Thermal conductivity, electrical conductivity and melting point, like density, are physical properties considered in material selection. Keep them distinct from mechanical hardness or toughness.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Thermal conductivity describes how readily heat is transmitted. The source gives examples of copper conducting heat better than aluminum, and stainless steel conducting it poorly. Heat sinks and heat exchangers seek to remove heat, while insulation seeks to retain it. Ease of conducting electricity and the amount of heat transmitted are separate properties.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Melting point relates to the temperature where a solid becomes liquid. Examples include high-melting-point tungsten and low-melting-point tin or solder. Do not determine service temperature from melting point alone; strength and structure can change while a material remains solid. Similar material names do not justify applying the values of a different alloy.

terms.meaning: A property indicating how readily heat is transmitted.
A value relating to the temperature of change from solid to liquid.
Surface brightness caused by light reflection.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-084.title: Distinguish heat-affected zones from forging flow lines
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-084.objective: Distinguish heat-affected zones from forging flow lines, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: Metal properties change when processing or heat treatment changes the structure. Welding can change structure by heat around the melted region too; this is a heat-affected zone. An area that did not melt does not necessarily retain the original properties. Check the required range and evaluation through specified inspection.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Forging flow lines are features related to material flow within a part formed by forging and similar processes. Impact direction and the direction of those lines may affect evaluation; shape alone does not determine strength. Changes to part orientation or stock layout require checking design and process approval.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: In bending a narrow strip, the source gives an example where a smaller bend radius concentrates the load on the outside and makes cracking more likely. Distinguish elastic recovery, retained plastic deformation, hardness and toughness. A single hardness result does not establish resistance to bend cracking or impact.

terms.meaning: A surrounding region whose structure or properties change from welding heat and similar causes.
A feature related to material flow produced by forging and similar processes.
The radius of a bent region.
